rv.q: Anchuli Felicia King's Singapore-set drama brilliantly unpicks hypocrisy and the base values of the beauty business.
Even where White Pearl feels cut short or cut shallow, it has a boldness, ambition and acerbic humour on a scale that makes you sit up and pay attention.
King writes with brio and cleverly uses comedy to shock and to open up layers of prejudice and assumption.
Yet WHITE PEARL as satire – the drama hinges on a racist ad that has gone viral – White Pearl is heavy-handed.
But it needs more clarity. At present, the only people likely to decode it are GCHQ Far East desk operatives.
Skin-whitening drama with a troublingly light tone...implausibilities abound and the denoument is abrupt.
There's substance to the satire of 'White Pearl,' but its set-ups are so flimsy, it soon falls apart.
This is a heartless, ill-plotted play by a writer who appears to loathe all the materials she has assembled: the characters, their jobs, their motives, their attitudes, and their use of language.

cn.t: King's sharp satire about a cosmetics crisis in Singapore divides critics with its machine-gun dialogue and timely themes, earning praise for deft writing but criticism for frenzied pacing and execution.
